messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — rt-queue-warning on runtime-usw2-3. Queue depth spiking, p50 latency > 750ms, 5xx rate rising to 6% over last 2m. Trigger: runtime-queue-threshold. Paging oncall @alice.k :rotating_light:
alice.k: I got it. I'm oncall and looking. Can someone confirm customer impact? Which routes are hottest?
ben.r: Observability: embed and streaming routes are producing most backpressure. Inflight count per-GPU hitting ~420 (config cap 500). KV cache hit dropped to 12%.
maya_sre: FYI thermal/power metrics are normal for the nodes, so it's not HW throttling. This looks like sudden request mix change.
alice.k: Quick mitigations I want to try in order: 1) apply temporary shedding to non-SLAs 2) lower per-request max_inflight to 300 3) disable streaming for bursty callers 4) raise short-term quota for dedicated customers if they are blocked. Any objections?
ben.r: +1. I can push the shedding rule and adjust max_inflight. Command I'm going to run in 30s: ```
# apply soft-shedding for best-effort traffic
redwoodctl traffic modify --pool runtime-usw2-3 --policy soft_shed --target label:priority=best-effort --threshold 75
# lower per-GPU in-flight cap
redwoodctl runtime set --pool runtime-usw2-3 --max-inflight 300
```
sam_support: I'll start triage with CS and surface any high-severity customer reports. Carla, can you check if any major customers are seeing 500s?
carla_cs: Checking now. Early scan: two mid-market customers (acct-142, acct-77) reported timeouts on embedding calls. No enterprise SLA claims yet. I'll prep an outbound note if mitigation doesn't fix in 10m.
ben.r: Pushing the commands now. 1) soft_shed applied 2) max_inflight set -> change propagated to 4/6 nodes, others pending.
alice.k: Good. Also toggle off streaming for non-enterprise routes: ```
redwoodctl feature toggle --pool runtime-usw2-3 --feature streaming --selector tier!=enterprise --state off
```
maya_sre: After the first changes: queue depth dropped ~40% on the affected pods. p50 latency back to ~420ms, 5xx down to 2.1%. Still higher than baseline but trending better.
alice.k: Nice. Keep monitoring for 5m. Ben, if 5xx <1% and latency stable, plan to roll back streaming toggle and increase max_inflight gradually.
ben.r: A few follow-ups: we saw one noisy customer (acct-9001) sending chaining stream requests; I applied a per-customer rate cap: ```
redwoodctl quota update --customer acct-9001 --rate 30rps
```
sam_support: CS will message acct-142 and acct-77 with the incident note and ETA: mitigations in progress. :white_check_mark:
carla_cs: Confirmed both saw reduced errors after soft-shed. No escalation needed yet.
maya_sre: Also created an alert to detect sudden KV-cache hit drops — that pattern correlated with today's spike. Filing follow-up action item for research.
alice.k: Good work. We'll keep the cap in place for 15m then reassess. If stable, we'll lift shedding and restore streaming for enterprise only, then stepwise for others.
ben.r: 15m timer started. I'll keep an eye and will post when we revert.
incident-bot: NOTE — incident state changed: mitigation_in_progress -> partial_recovery at 4487654375
alice.k: Partial recovery confirmed. Moving to monitoring phase. I'll keep watch and handoff to the next oncall in 25m if stable.
carla_cs: CS note sent to impacted customers. Will update if we get further reports.
ben.r: Reverting streaming toggle for enterprise routes now, leaving best-effort shed in place until morning.
maya_sre: Filed follow-up playbook update: add quick checklist for sudden embedding storms + auto-apply per-customer soft caps when per-gpu inflight > 80%.
alice.k: Thanks all — closing pager in 10m if no regression. :thumbsup:
